turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about that zero on his phone in the middle of a class and nobody called me, so start with who decided that, and when.
I don't think this is productive.
Productive. You entered a zero on Owen's essay without calling me, and you asked for this meeting, so answer the question or I walk upstairs to the principal's office. Who decided, and when?
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

Then you have ten minutes, and I'm not leaving this chair until you've used them. Your own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody contacted me. Either you tell me now on what basis that zero went in, or I'm in the principal's office before your bell rings.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

I'm writing down that you said "I'm done here" without answering one question about Owen's zero. I won't be emailing anyone, Hale, I'll be standing in the principal's office in five minutes. The zero comes off, and nothing about this goes on his record.
